title: Grid Systems in Graphic Design
lede: Josef Müller-Brockmann’s manual of the grid, with the grid itself drawn on its cover.
summary: Josef Müller-Brockmann, Niggli, 1981. The standard handbook of the typographic grid.

source.label: eMuseum, Museum für Gestaltung Zürich: A JMBR 181-1-6

evidence.note: Downloaded the cover scan [File:Raster-Systeme-Cover.jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Raster-Systeme-Cover.jpg) (1200 × 1663 px) to a scratch folder and inspected it. Interior pages were not seen. The image is not stored.

styles.note: A late summary of the style’s central method by one of its founders; the grid on the cover is the style’s structure made explicit.

context: *Rastersysteme für die visuelle Gestaltung / Grid systems in graphic design*, 1981; bilingual German and English, subtitled a handbook for graphic designers, typographers, and exhibition designers. The eMuseum holds the cover and several cover drafts from the Müller-Brockmann archive, donated by Shizuko Yoshikawa. [eMuseum object 167597](https://www.emuseum.ch/objects/167597).

Wikipedia’s bibliography lists it as published by Arthur Niggli, Niederteufen, 1981, ISBN 9783721201451. [Wikipedia: Josef Müller-Brockmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josef_M%C3%BCller-Brockmann).
Müller-Brockmann was a founding editor of [Neue Grafik](ref:neue-grafik-journal-1958-1965) and designed [Der Film](ref:der-film-poster-1960).
observed: The cover is a flat orange with a grid of thin white lines: four columns and several rows separated by narrow gutters.
Black grotesque type sits exactly on the grid. The two titles, “Grid systems” and “Raster systeme”, are the largest elements and start at the left margin.
Subtitles and the author’s name are small and flush left, starting either at the left margin or at the third column line.
The publisher’s name “Niggli” sits alone near the bottom, on the same column line as the author’s name.
Only three colors appear: orange, black, and white.
interpretation: Showing the grid lines on the cover makes the invisible structure of the style visible, and turns a method into an image.
borrow: Start text blocks on only two or three column lines, and repeat those lines throughout the layout.
Consider revealing the grid as thin lines when the subject is structure or documentation.
Use one saturated flat background color with black type and white rules.

rights.statement: Wikimedia Commons marks its cover scan as public domain; this catalogue does not rely on that claim. The book remains in copyright; no image is stored.
